task.title: Canonical typed query keys
task.specification: Config empty. Every event is encode{value}, where value is JSON null/boolean/safe integer/string/array/object, maximum depth 3; object keys are single lowercase ASCII letters. Output {key:canonical_JSON_string}. Canonical JSON has no insignificant spaces; recursively sort object keys lexically, preserve array order, encode strings and scalars exactly as ECMAScript JSON.stringify: quote and backslash escaped, backspace/form-feed/newline/carriage-return/tab use their short escapes, other U+0000..U+001F characters use lowercase four-digit Unicode escapes, and all other Unicode (including U+2028/U+2029) and slash remain literal. Emit null/true/false/numbers without added type coercion. Unicode string values are allowed; no lone surrogates, nonintegral numbers or negative zero occur. State is irrelevant. Distinctions between absent and null, numeric and string values, boolean and integer, or array order must remain distinguishable. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}, initially state=null. Only the current event is supplied; every named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"restore"}. Return exactly the stated output fields each step; opaque JSON state is not graded. All numeric inputs and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; time deltas are nonnegative. Unless a task explicitly overrides this, keys, snapshot IDs, readers and graph nodes are single lowercase ASCII letters. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. At most eight identities and 48 events occur. Configurations and event fields shown below are present. Ordinary regimes use moderate storage and timing; boundary uses equality/empty states; adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events; shift uses smaller capacity, longer timing gaps or deeper dependency shapes, without changing these rules. Generator regimes: Shift permits nested values of depth three versus ordinary depth two; typed scalar distinctions remain required. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Astronomical interferometry
matchedCard.relation: Separated measurements can be combined after their relative arrival paths are aligned. Different separations and orientations contribute different spatial information; fine detail and broad structure require complementary measurement coverage.
assumptions: The measurements concern a compatible signal and maintain the needed relative alignment.
The range of separations and orientations samples the structure being reconstructed.
matchedCard.boundary: A longer separation does not supply missing measurement orientations or increase the collecting area by the same factor. Misaligned signals need not combine into an accurate reconstruction.
matchedCard.source_fact: ESO describes compensating path delays in interferometry and reconstructing images from telescope baselines of different lengths and orientations, distinguishing resolution from collected light.

shuffledCard.label: Canal locks
shuffledCard.relation: Passage between regions at different levels proceeds through an intermediate chamber. The chamber matches the entrance level before admission, is isolated while its level changes, and matches the departure level before release.
assumptions: The chamber can be isolated from each neighboring region.
Level differences and the states of the gates are observable.
shuffledCard.boundary: Simultaneous open connections bypass the intermediate isolation. An unobserved level difference does not establish that opening a gate is appropriate.
shuffledCard.source_fact: USACE describes raising and lowering vessels by closing lock gates, filling or emptying the chamber, and opening the gates after levels equalize.

initial.explanation: Each encode event independently maps its value to a canonical JSON serialization. Objects are recursively key-sorted; arrays retain order; scalars preserve their JSON types and values. State is unchanged and irrelevant.

initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;function q(v){if(v===null)return'null';if(typeof v==='string')return'"'+v.replace(/[\\"\u0000-\u001f]/g,function(c){return({'\\':'\\\\','"':'\\"','\b':'\\b','\f':'\\f','\n':'\\n','\r':'\\r','\t':'\\t'})[c]||'\\u'+c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).padStart(4,'0')})+'"';if(typeof v==='number'||typeof v==='boolean')return String(v);if(Array.isArray(v))return'['+v.map(q)+']';return'{'+Object.keys(v).sort().map(function(k){return q(k)+':'+q(v[k])}).join(',')+'}'}for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++)if(!input.events[i]||input.events[i].type!=='encode'||!output[i]||output[i].key!==q(input.events[i].value))return false;return true}

final.explanation: Each event is serialized independently. Scalars use their JSON representations, strings receive ECMAScript-compatible escaping, arrays preserve order, and objects are recursively serialized after lexical key sorting. The opaque state remains null.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){function enc(v){if(v===null)return"null";var t=typeof v;if(t==="string")return'"'+v.replace(/[\\"\u0000-\u001f]/g,function(c){if(c==='\\')return'\\\\';if(c==='"')return'\\"';if(c==='\b')return'\\b';if(c==='\f')return'\\f';if(c==='\n')return'\\n';if(c==='\r')return'\\r';if(c==='\t')return'\\t';return'\\u'+c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).padStart(4,'0')})+'"';if(t==='number'||t==='boolean')return String(v);if(Array.isArray(v)){var a=[];for(var i=0;i<v.length;i++)a.push(enc(v[i]));return'['+a.join(',')+']'}var k=Object.keys(v).sort(),a=[];for(var j=0;j<k.length;j++)a.push(enc(k[j])+':'+enc(v[k[j]]));return'{'+a.join(',')+'}'}return{state:null,output:{key:enc(event.value)}}}

initial.explanation: For every encode event, recursively serialize the supplied JSON value canonically: object keys are lexically sorted, arrays retain order, and primitive spellings follow ECMAScript JSON.stringify. Return that string under key and preserve no meaningful state.
initial.mapping: The event value maps to output.key through recursive canonical encoding; state is intentionally irrelevant.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated JSON-value, depth, key, and numeric restrictions. JSON.stringify provides the specified scalar and string escaping behavior.
initial.program: function solve(x){function c(v){if(v===null||typeof v!=='object')return JSON.stringify(v);if(Array.isArray(v)){var a=new Array(v.length);for(var i=0;i<v.length;i++)a[i]=c(v[i]);return '['+a.join(',')+']'}var k=Object.keys(v).sort(),a=new Array(k.length);for(var j=0;j<k.length;j++)a[j]=JSON.stringify(k[j])+':'+c(v[k[j]]);return '{'+a.join(',')+'}'}return {state:null,output:{key:c(x.event.value)}}}

final.explanation: Recursively canonicalize each event value. Arrays preserve order, while object keys are sorted lexically before serialization. JSON.stringify supplies the required ECMAScript representation for strings, booleans, null, and numbers. The state remains null because it is irrelevant.
final.program: function solve(x){function encode(v){if(v===null||typeof v!=='object')return JSON.stringify(v);if(Array.isArray(v)){var a=new Array(v.length);for(var i=0;i<v.length;i++)a[i]=encode(v[i]);return '['+a.join(',')+']'}var keys=Object.keys(v).sort(),parts=new Array(keys.length);for(var j=0;j<keys.length;j++){var k=keys[j];parts[j]=JSON.stringify(k)+':'+encode(v[k])}return '{'+parts.join(',')+'}'}return {state:null,output:{key:encode(x.event.value)}}}

initial.program: function esc(s){var r='"';for(var i=0;i<s.length;i++){var c=s.charCodeAt(i);if(c===34)r+='\\"';else if(c===92)r+='\\\\';else if(c===8)r+='\\b';else if(c===12)r+='\\f';else if(c===10)r+='\\n';else if(c===13)r+='\\r';else if(c===9)r+='\\t';else if(c<32){var h=c.toString(16);r+='\\u'+('0000'+h).slice(-4);}else r+=s[i];}return r+'"';}function enc(v){if(v===null)return'null';var t=typeof v;if(t==='string')return esc(v);if(t==='boolean'||t==='number')return JSON.stringify(v);if(Array.isArray(v)){var a=[];for(var i=0;i<v.length;i++)a.push(enc(v[i]));return'['+a.join(',')+']';}var k=Object.keys(v).sort(),a=[];for(var j=0;j<k.length;j++)a.push(esc(k[j])+':'+enc(v[k[j]]));return'{'+a.join(',')+'}';}function solve(x){return{state:null,output:{key:enc(x.event.value)}};}
